anchor.quote: Let $f$ be the parameter of a call
Here $m$ is the factor by which the parameter grows
Let $s$ be the number of subcalls of one call.
Let $\Phi(f)$ be the cost of a call divided by the volume $V$ it works on.
Let $C$ be a constant such that the call's own outside work is at most $C(mf)^\lambda$
An address interchange of $u$-bit fields costs $O(Vu^\tau)$, where $\tau<1$ is fixed.
Here $\Omega$ is the bit count of one axis chunk
Let $\nu$ count the levels of unrolling

anchor.note: Only a range is given; the page never says that sigma is an auxiliary exponent bounding the weight (s/W)^nu by m^(nu sigma). Earlier pages bind sigma to other things (row of a one, last-axis exponent).
Big-O notation, covered by the undergraduate asymptotic analysis background (the letter O also names the odd sub-transform on the DFT page, but here it is asymptotic).
Summation notation and geometric series, covered by the calculus and discrete mathematics background.

gaps.note: Wrong value: 2^0.8 is about 1.741, so (3/2)/2^0.8 is about 0.861, not 1.16 (1.16 is its reciprocal). It must be below 1, as the page says for any lambda > log_m(s/W) ~ 0.585; 1.16 would contradict that and the convergence claim.

Does not follow. With d^vartheta <= f only, f^sigma d^{vartheta(1-sigma)} can be as large as f, which exceeds f^lambda (e.g. f near d^vartheta gives d^{vartheta(1-sigma)} vs d^{vartheta(lambda-sigma)}). The paper (lines 2423-2444) only bounds the leaves by O(e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)}) and absorbs them in the final exponent lambda' > max{lambda, sigma+beta(1-sigma)}, so the overall bound is O(d^lambda'), not O(f^lambda).

gaps.quote: Since $\vartheta=\tfrac12$ is a fixed exponent, $d\le f^{1/\vartheta}$
gaps.note: Being a fixed exponent does not give this inequality. It holds only at internal nodes, where f >= d^vartheta (paper line 2413), and that stopping rule is introduced only in the next paragraph. The hypothesis is missing at the point of use.

gaps.quote: The leaves at depth $\nu$ have $u=f/m^\nu<d^\vartheta$ chunks
gaps.note: Here u counts chunks, whereas earlier on the same page u is a number of bits of a field (u = f Omega bits) and it is the field width of the address-fields page. The page flags other letter changes but not this one, so the reader cannot tell the two uses apart.

gaps.quote: Each leaf is handled by one kernel per chunk
gaps.note: Kernel is never defined on the page or in the reader's known concepts. In the paper it is the individual selected-bit C kernel (a 2x2 butterfly on one address bit), costing O(V) per kernel; the reader cannot see why the leaf cost is O(f/m^nu).

gaps.quote: The outside work is a fixed number of address-field row additions.
gaps.note: The page asserts that the outside work (changes of basis, scalar gates, corrections, reassembly) reduces to a fixed number of row additions and that a row addition costs O(V(u^tau+1)), but it only cites the cost of an interchange. Neither why the count is fixed nor why a row addition has the same cost is given (the paper derives these at lines 2268-2290 from the fixed network and a separate lemma).
